# Image Consent Checklist

> Complete this for **every photograph** before it is uploaded to the Studio.
> Not per batch — per image. One image without consent taints the whole record.
>
> Consent is about a person's control over their own likeness. It is not a
> formality, and it is not something a photograph of a smiling crowd at a
> community event can be assumed to carry.

---

## The one rule that overrides everything

> **If you cannot produce written consent for an image, that image is not
> published.** There is no exception for a good photo, an outreach that is
> going well, a busy schedule, a person who said yes in passing, or a person
> who is not available to ask again. Set the image to `Not for publication` and
> move on.

---

## Part 1 — Before the photograph is taken

Ask at the point of taking the photograph, not afterwards. Consent obtained
after somebody has seen themselves in a photograph is rarely free.

- [ ] At the start of the session or talk, I explained that NHECOF photographs
      activities and may publish the photographs on its website and social media
- [ ] I said what NHECOF does with the photographs: website, printed materials,
      social media, and reports to funders
- [ ] I said how long they may be kept and how to ask for removal later
- [ ] I said they can decline, and that declining will not affect their care,
      their place in the session, or any benefit they receive from NHECOF
- [ ] I did not photograph anyone who asked not to be photographed
- [ ] I did not photograph anyone who seemed not to understand what I was asking
- [ ] For a group photo, I checked that nobody left part-way through and that
      nobody objected

**Who took part in this briefing?** _______________________________________

---

## Part 2 — Before the photograph is uploaded

**For each image, work through this:**

- [ ] I know who is in it
- [ ] I know who took it
- [ ] I can find the written consent paperwork for it
- [ ] The file is under about 2 MB
- [ ] Featured and hero images are at least 1200 px wide
- [ ] Landscape orientation for feature images
- [ ] Filename is meaningful, not `IMG_4821.jpg`
- [ ] It does not contain anybody's name, face and medical information together
- [ ] It does not show a screening result, a blood-pressure reading, a weight, a
      test result, a prescription or a medical record

**Last one deserves repeating.** A photograph of a health-screening table with
a participant's results visible is not a usable photograph. Retake it, or crop
it so no result is readable, or do not use it. There is no consent that makes
publishing an individual's result acceptable.

---

## Part 3 — The rules for images of children

> **Anyone under 18. This is not a judgement call about who looks old enough.**

### The Studio fields

1. Tick **"Does this image show anyone under 18?"** → **Yes**
2. The Studio then reveals **"Guardian Consent Recorded"**
3. Tick it **only** when a parent or guardian has agreed **in writing**

The Studio refuses to publish an image of a minor without that tick. Do not
work around this.

### What the written guardian consent must contain

- [ ] The child's name or, if the record is anonymised, a clear description
- [ ] The parent's or guardian's name
- [ ] The relationship to the child
- [ ] The date of the event
- [ ] What the photograph shows
- [ ] Explicit permission for NHECOF to publish it **on its website**
- [ ] Explicit permission for **social media** use
- [ ] A signature, and a phone number or email to reach them
- [ ] A statement that they can ask for the image to be removed at any time, and
      how to do so

### A verbal yes is not consent

- [ ] The agreement is **written and signed**. A guardian saying "yes, take the
      photograph" at the event is not sufficient and must not be recorded as
      consent.

### When written guardian consent does not exist

- [ ] The image is set to **`Not for publication`**
- [ ] The image is not used — anywhere, including social media, printed reports
      and fundraising materials
- [ ] The image is left in the record rather than deleted, so the paperwork
      trail survives

### If you have no consent, prefer these instead

- Photograph hands, cooking, materials, or the activity rather than faces
- Photograph from behind, or from a distance where no child is individually
  identifiable
- Photograph a group from the back, or a wide shot
- Use no photograph at all — an honest record with no pictures is better than a
  record that puts a child at risk

**Never** crop, blur or otherwise disguise a child's face to get around a
consent requirement. Not publishing the image is the only acceptable answer.

---

## Part 4 — The rules for images of pregnant women, breastfeeding mothers, and women in traditional or private dress

> These are adults, so the under-18 rules do not apply and the Studio has no
> separate tick box for them. The rule below is therefore enforced by people,
> not by the software. It is no less strict.

### 1. Written consent, on the same basis

- [ ] Consent is **written and signed**, using the same form
- [ ] The guardian fields are left blank, because she is an adult
- [ ] She is told specifically that her photograph may appear on NHECOF's
      website and social media, permanently
- [ ] She is given the contact details for asking for removal later
- [ ] Her consent is matched to the right photograph — if she consented to one
      photo, that is consent for that photo

### 2. The pregnancy-specific rule: no health information, ever

- [ ] **No antenatal, blood-pressure, weight, sugar or screening result appears
      in the image**
- [ ] No clinic card, test result, patient number or medical record is visible
- [ ] No image shows a consultation in progress in a way that would identify a
      patient's condition
- [ ] If a photograph was taken during a screening session, it is not used
- [ ] Only aggregate figures — "42 women screened" — are ever published

> This rule cannot be waived. Nobody's written consent makes it acceptable to
> publish her individual medical information, and doing so could expose her to
> harm at home, at work, or in her community.

### 3. Modesty and dignity

- [ ] Nothing is photographed or published that the woman would not be comfortable
      with the whole community seeing
- [ ] Traditional dress, religious dress and body covering are respected, and not
      used in a way that invites comment
- [ ] She was asked before the photograph, not after
- [ ] The photograph is not used in a fundraising context without her specific
      agreement to that use

### 4. When in doubt

- [ ] The image is not used
- [ ] Another image is used instead
- [ ] The uncertainty is raised with the outreach manager before the record is
      published, not afterwards

## Part 5 — Uploading: the Studio fields

Complete for every image:

| Field | Entry |
| --- | --- |
| **Alt text** | |
| **Decorative** | ☐ Yes ☐ No |
| **Caption** | |
| **Credit** (photographer, or `NHECOF`) | |
| **Consent Status** | ☐ Cleared ☐ Pending ☐ Not for publication |
| **Shows anyone under 18?** | ☐ Yes ☐ No |
| **Guardian Consent Recorded** | ☐ Yes ☐ No *(only appears if above is Yes)* |

### Writing alt text

Describe **what is happening**, for somebody who cannot see the photograph.

- **Good:** "A health worker measuring a woman's blood pressure at a community outreach"
- **Bad:** "IMG_4021.jpg"
- **Bad:** "A happy family" — vague, and it may not be their family
- **Bad:** "Image of a person" — useless

- [ ] Alt text does not name anybody, because the caption or credit is where a
      name goes
- [ ] Alt text is under about 125 characters
- [ ] **Decorative** is ticked only for pure decoration, such as a background
      shape. An informative image marked decorative loses its alt text and
      becomes invisible to screen-reader users.

## Part 6 — Where the paperwork lives

- [ ] Consent forms are filed, and I know where
- [ ] The filing location is recorded on the outreach record
- [ ] Forms are not kept only on a phone that can be lost
- [ ] There is a named person responsible for consent records

**Consent forms are stored at:** _______________________________________

**Responsible person:** _______________________________________________

> Do not store consent forms in the Sanity dataset. It is not a secure place for
> signed agreements containing a child's name and a guardian's signature.

---

## Part 7 — Known gaps to be aware of

These are real limitations of the current website, not of this checklist. They
are recorded here so nobody relies on the software to catch them.

1. **On the outreach page, image consent is not enforced by the website.** The
   page displays the photographs attached to an outreach record and assumes
   consent has been given, rather than checking the `Consent Status` field. Until
   this is fixed, the person setting the field is the only protection. Set it
   correctly.
2. **The social-sharing image has no consent fields at all.** A separate image
   chooser appears under SEO Metadata. It is not connected to this system. Do not
   use a photograph of a child, or of a recognisable person, there.
3. **The prohibited-word check does not run on image captions or alt text.** Scan
   them yourself.
